findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tag the review-vote/submission AC with [operator-attested] (or point it at the recorded change-id/vote) so its out-of-codebase evidence is graded as a concrete attestation.
evidence: The vote/submission outcome is a Gerrit process artifact, not a repo artifact evaluable by the agent in-session
findings.finding: The final AC requires each change to earn 'LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and is submitted' — evidence that lives outside the codebase — but the checkbox is not tagged [operator-attested], leaving its in-session completability ambiguous.
findings.location: AC: 'each change earns LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and is submitted before this ticket closes'
scenarios: Agent cannot self-satisfy the vote+submit criterion within one working session; grading needs a recorded attestation

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Change 1's _submit_ctx rationale: _in_gate_session/_active_code_root are defined in llm/gate_context.py (re-exported via llm/config.py), not in generation.py — restate the placement justification on the verified grounds (docstring reference + shared-by-both-callers cycle avoidance).
evidence: Plan: '_submit_ctx moves to generation.py ... It belongs in generation.py on the merits — its job is carrying that module's gate-session ContextVars (_in_gate_session, _active_code_root) into pool workers'
gate_context.py:170 '_in_gate_session: contextvars.ContextVar[bool]' and gate_context.py:65 '_active_code_root: contextvars.ContextVar' — the ContextVars live here, not in generation.py
generation.py:120 defines a DIFFERENT ContextVar (_CANCEL_SCOPE); grep for _in_gate_session/_active_code_root in generation.py returns no matches

The independent, verified justifications (generation.py already names pass1._submit_ctx in its docstring at line 131; _submit_ctx is shared by both _run_container@290 and run_pass1@578-579 so leaving it in pass1 would cycle) still hold — only the 'merits/ownership' rationale is wrong
findings.finding: Change 1's merits-based justification for relocating _submit_ctx to generation.py rests on a false premise: it claims _submit_ctx's job is 'carrying that module's [generation.py's] gate-session ContextVars (_in_gate_session / _active_code_root)', but those two ContextVars are defined in src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py (re-exported via llm/config.py), NOT in generation.py. generation.py owns a different ContextVar (_CANCEL_SCOPE). So the sentence 'It belongs in generation.py on the merits — its job is carrying that module's ... ContextVars' is factually wrong about ownership; the ContextVars belong to gate_context.py.
findings.location: Change 1 — pass1.py, the '_submit_ctx moves to generation.py' paragraph
scenarios: An author relies on the stated rationale to justify placement and then finds generation.py has no gate-session ContextVar to co-locate with, revisiting the extraction target
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'its job is carrying that module's gate-session ContextVars' with 'its job is carrying the gate-session ContextVars (defined in llm/gate_context.py, re-exported via llm/config.py) into pool workers'; keep the cycle-avoidance and docstring-reference arguments as the placement basis.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the _submit_ctx placement rationale: _in_gate_session/_active_code_root live in llm/gate_context.py, not generation.py — justify the move by generation.review_cancelled() running inside the pool worker (and the existing pass1._submit_ctx docstring reference) instead.
evidence: Plan: '_submit_ctx moves to generation.py ... its job is carrying that module's gate-session ContextVars (_in_gate_session, _active_code_root) into pool workers'
src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py:65 defines _active_code_root and :170 defines _in_gate_session (config.py:49/51 imports both FROM gate_context)
generation.py's only module-level ContextVar is _CANCEL_SCOPE (generation.py:120); its pass1._submit_ctx reference is a docstring mention (generation.py:131)
findings.finding: Change 1's positive rationale for relocating _submit_ctx to generation.py misidentifies where the gate-session ContextVars live: it claims _submit_ctx 'belongs in generation.py on the merits — its job is carrying that module's gate-session ContextVars (_in_gate_session / _active_code_root)', but those two ContextVars are defined in llm/gate_context.py (re-exported via llm/config.py), not in generation.py. generation.py's own run-scoped ContextVar is _CANCEL_SCOPE. The move still works mechanically (copy_context() is agnostic to which module owns the vars) and the placement is defensible on other grounds (generation.review_cancelled() is invoked inside the pool worker, and generation.py's docstring already names pass1._submit_ctx), so this is a rationale-accuracy defect, not a mechanism defect.
findings.location: Change 1 — 'Extract to container_stage.py' paragraph, sentence beginning 'It belongs in generation.py on the merits'
scenarios: An implementer trusts the stated rationale, places _submit_ctx expecting generation.py to own those vars, and is later confused when the real ownership (gate_context.py) surfaces during test or review
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: '_submit_ctx belongs with generation.py because the worker it launches invokes generation.review_cancelled() (mid-run cancellation) and copy_context() must capture that generation-owned _CANCEL_SCOPE; the gate-session vars it also carries live in gate_context.py and are captured generically.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the test that asserts the near-cap pass emits the expected warnings for an in-band file AND that the gate step exits 0 when the list is non-empty (guarding AC-6's non-blocking contract).
evidence: 'Append to that same step a NON-BLOCKING pass emitting one `::warning::` annotation per src/rebar file within a headroom band of the locked cap, exiting 0 regardless.'
AC: 'still passes when that list is non-empty' — a behavioral claim
Verification section lists test_module_size_contract.py and full CI suite but does not name a test exercising the new near-cap warning path
findings.finding: Change 3 introduces new CI behavior — a non-blocking near-cap warning pass that emits one `::warning::` per file in a headroom band and must exit 0 even when the list is non-empty — but the verification section names no test asserting the exit-0-on-non-empty-band contract; AC-6's falsifiable claim ('still passes when that list is non-empty') has no proof path.
findings.location: Change 3; AC line 'The CI module-size gate emits a non-blocking near-cap warning ... and still passes when that list is non-empty.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test (or extend test_module_size_contract.py) that runs the gate step against a fixture with a file in the headroom band and asserts both the ::warning:: emission and a zero exit status.

evidence: verify command `find | wc -l` inspects output with `find` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact near-cap band rule (e.g. files with LOC in [cap-20, cap]) so the warning's file set is deterministic and the AC is checkable.
evidence: 'emitting one ::warning:: annotation per src/rebar file within a headroom band of the locked cap'
'the band derives from the locked limit, not a second magic number' — but the derivation formula/width is never given
AC: 'listing every file in the headroom band'
findings.finding: Change 3's 'headroom band' has no stated numeric width, so an executor cannot determine which files the non-blocking warning must list.
findings.location: Change 3; AC 'lists every file in the headroom band'
scenarios: Executor must pick a band boundary (e.g. >=680? >=690?) to write the gate step and cannot without guessing
findings.suggested_fix: Define the band as a fixed offset from the locked cap, e.g. 'warn on any src/rebar file with LOC >= cap-25', and reference that single derivation in both the gate step and the AC.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive build_sibling_roster's reference inventory with find_referencing_symbols AND a string grep, add eval_solver.py (`from ...pass1 import build_sibling_roster`) and fidelity_spot_eval.py (`pass1.build_sibling_roster`) to Change 1's compatibility list, and state that the module-level re-export explicitly preserves build_sibling_roster for both.
evidence: Plan enumerates importers as only 'orchestrator.py imports ... and provider_parity.py imports CONTAINER_CRITERIA — both preserved by module-level re-export.'
Plan lists build_sibling_roster among symbols extracted to container_stage.py.
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:101: `from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA, build_sibling_roster` — a from-import requiring build_sibling_roster as a pass1 module attribute.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:223: `roster = pass1.build_sibling_roster(children)` — attribute access on the pass1 module.
tests/unit/test_container_roster.py:110-112 asserts 'build_sibling_roster' in inspect.getsource(eval_solver) and (fidelity_spot_eval), the source-text tests tied to these two call sites.
findings.finding: Change 1's compatibility inventory for the moved symbol build_sibling_roster is incomplete: it enumerates only orchestrator.py and provider_parity.py as consumers to preserve via re-export, but two other modules reference build_sibling_roster directly — eval_solver.py:101 (`from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA, build_sibling_roster`) and fidelity_spot_eval.py:223 (`pass1.build_sibling_roster(children)`).
findings.location: Change 1 — 'orchestrator.py imports CONTAINER_CRITERIA, _run_container, _ticket_graph_blob, material_fingerprint from .pass1 and provider_parity.py imports CONTAINER_CRITERIA — both preserved by module-level re-export.'
scenarios: eval_solver.py's top-level `from ...pass1 import build_sibling_roster` raises ImportError at import time if the pass1 re-export list (derived from the incomplete importer enumeration) omits build_sibling_roster — breaking the inline-fixture eval path.
fidelity_spot_eval.py:223's `pass1.build_sibling_roster(children)` raises AttributeError if the re-export omits the symbol — breaking the container spot-eval harness.

Because these two consumers were not surfaced in the inventory, test_container_roster.py::test_roster_builder_single_sourced (which greps eval_solver/fidelity_spot_eval source) is not accounted for as a consumer dependency, risking an under-scoped re-export.
findings.suggested_fix: Add build_sibling_roster to the re-exported symbols and note both consumers: 'eval_solver.py does `from ...pass1 import build_sibling_roster` and fidelity_spot_eval.py calls `pass1.build_sibling_roster`; both preserved by the module-level re-export.'
